newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty calls for end to killings in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty calls for end to killings in Cambodia.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Thursday there is compelling evidence that the new regime in Cambodia has a "targeted campaign" to eliminate political opponents.

The London-based human rights group said it believed a second senior member of the royalist FUNCINPEC party loyal to ousted prime minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh had been killed in custody and at least five others have died.
"The apparent killing in custody...is compelling evidence of a targeted campaign to eliminate political opponents," Amnesty said in a statement.

"We believe Chao Sambath was killed yesterday. We know Hor Sok was killed on Monday. There must be no more killings. Assurances from senior political figures that no one is being targeted ring hollow after these events."
Ranariddh was ousted on Sunday by his co-prime minister Hun Sen after two days of fighting between their forces in the capital Phnom Penh.

Ranariddh left for France on the eve of the violence. On Thursday he appealed to the Security Council of the United Nations in New York not to recognise any new government and to order a freeze on aid to Cambodia. Amnesty said it had also received reports from eye witnesses claiming that the bodies of four other men, believed to have been former body guards of Chao Sambath, were left at a temple in the captial and they had been handcuffed and gagged and had gunshot wounds.

"People have been summarily executed, appparently solely on account of whom they once worked for. The exodus of prominent political figures from Cambodia will continue, as long as they remain in fear of their lives," Amnesty predicted.

The group welcomed the stance of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) which has assisted in the safe passage of people at risk, and its decision to postpone Cambodia's membership and to continue to recognise Ranariddh as co-premier.
Amnesty said it was also concerned about the safety of people held in detention, including hundreds of FUNCINPEC soldiers and officials, who have been held since last weekend.
It urged the Cambodian authorities to grant officials from the International Committee of the Red Cross and the United Nations Centre for Human Rights access to the detainees.
